questions.q: What makes a balance "past due" rather than simply "outstanding"?
options: Past due just means the invoice amount is over $10,000
There is no difference between the two terms
Past due requires the due_date to have already passed, in addition to there being an amount still owed
Past due means the customer has made at least one payment
questions.explain: Outstanding only means not fully paid; past due additionally requires the due date to already be in the past, as enforced by `due_date < TRUNC(SYSDATE)`.

questions.q: In Investigation 1, what does `WHERE ps.amount_due_remaining > 0 AND ps.due_date < TRUNC(SYSDATE)` isolate?
options: Every transaction regardless of payment status
Only fully paid transactions
Transactions due in the future
Transactions with money still owed AND whose due date has already passed — i.e., truly past due
questions.explain: Both conditions must be true together: an outstanding amount greater than zero, and a due date that has already passed.

questions.q: What reconciliation pattern does Investigation 2 (unapplied cash by customer) reuse from Lesson 21?
options: LEFT OUTER JOIN plus an NVL-guarded difference, filtered with HAVING <> 0
CASE-based aging buckets
ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by customer
The MINUS set operator
questions.explain: Investigation 2 directly reapplies Lesson 21's reconciliation pattern: outer join, NVL-guard the aggregate, then HAVING the difference not equal to zero.

questions.q: In Investigation 3, what does combining EXISTS and NOT EXISTS in the same query accomplish?
options: It cancels both conditions out, returning every row
It finds customers who both HAVE at least one transaction AND have NEVER made a cash receipt
It is invalid syntax — EXISTS and NOT EXISTS cannot appear in the same WHERE clause
It only checks for transactions, ignoring cash receipts entirely
questions.explain: EXISTS confirms the customer has at least one transaction, while NOT EXISTS confirms they have zero cash receipts — both conditions must hold together.

questions.q: Why does Investigation 1 use FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY after ORDER BY total_past_due DESC?
options: To return the 5 smallest past-due balances
FETCH FIRST has no effect when combined with GROUP BY
To randomly sample 5 rows from the result
To cap the sorted result to the top 5 customers by past-due exposure
questions.explain: FETCH FIRST applies after the ORDER BY sort, correctly returning the 5 customers with the largest past-due totals.
